title: HistoryV2
description: A history of sessions: the ordered steps of one or more sessions of an application whose guest is the session world hologram:guest/core-wasm@2, each step with the responses it returned. A session starts with an empty state on a fresh instance, so its responses are a function of its ordered requests; a failure ends the session and is its last record. Replay re-executes every session on a fresh instance and compares outcomes byte for byte. Its digests cover its canonical JSON with no trailing newline. prism/history/1 keeps its meaning for the stateless world. Design: docs/proposals/629-session-world.md.

application.description: The name of the application when it was recorded, or null. Information for a person; replay never compares it.

recordedFrom.description: The build the history was recorded from. Information for a person; replay never compares it, because the point of a replay is to run a different build.

sessions.description: The sessions in the order they were recorded. A history of nothing proves nothing, so at least one is required.

Session.description: One session: its steps in order, and the failure that ended it, if one did. A session records at least one step or a failure.

Step.description: A step that returned: its request and the responses it returned, in order. A step may return no response.

Failure.description: The step that ended the session in a refusal or a trap, named by its stable code. No step follows it.

Hex.description: Bytes as lowercase hex, two characters each. Hex has one spelling per value, so a digest has one meaning.

PrismDigestSet.description: sha256, the κ of the bytes (ADR-017); blake3 beside it only in statements and documents about a v4 holo (ADR-015). Lowercase hex.
